checked_sources.evidence: IAU table lists Sextans with abbreviation Sex. Its explanation says constellations are scientifically defined areas of sky and “in” means inside the defined boundary, not membership of a star pattern.

NASA identifies Caldwell 53 as NGC 3115: Sextans, 32 million light-years, lenticular galaxy, disk and bulge without spiral arms, edge-on appearance, and central black hole roughly one billion solar masses.

Actually opened. Submitted 9 Aug 2025; VLA localizes a faint 22-GHz nucleus in NGC 3115. Modeling the radio peak as an ADAF yields (1.2±0.2)×10^9 solar masses, consistent with prior 1–2×10^9 dynamical estimates.

evidence.finding: All factual claims and support metadata match. The text preserves the inferential status of the radio/ADAF mass estimate.
evidence.nonblocking_pedagogy: The self-check is sound but repeats the map-versus-physical-system distinction. If revised later, ask what the 1.2-billion-solar-mass result is based on (a modeled radio peak, not a direct image).

checked_sources.evidence: IAU table lists Volans with abbreviation Vol; the same source defines IAU constellations as bounded sky areas rather than physical groups.

Actually opened ESO release (4 May 2011): NGC 2442 is in Volans, has asymmetric spiral arms/double-hook appearance, and a gravitational interaction is thought likely, while the responsible galaxy is not positively identified.

Actually opened. Submitted 9 Sep 2026. The abstract combines radio continuum with optical H-alpha and infrared data; reports a southeast steep-spectrum synchrotron island with no clear H-alpha/IR/FUV/NUV counterpart; 2D simulations find anisotropic diffusion along ordered magnetic fields enables CREs to reach it more efficiently.

evidence.finding: All factual claims and support metadata match. “could” and the final caveat correctly avoid treating the transport model as a traced path for individual particles.
evidence.nonblocking_pedagogy: The current self-check is correct but duplicate in structure. If revising later, ask why a synchrotron island can be visible without clear local young-star tracers: the paper infers CREs are unlikely to be injected there and models transport from elsewhere.
